clauses.reason: Section 4 provides that the Coat of Arms, Seal and Color and Flag shall be as described and as set forth in the attached illustrations and specifications, and that the designs shall be used to represent the Vice President of the United States exclusively. It has no end date or ending condition of its own and nothing held amends, revokes or supersedes it, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

Section 5 states that the order becomes effective immediately and revokes Executive Order No. 10016 of November 10, 1948, in the present tense (is hereby revoked). Both effects were performed by the order itself when the President signed it on October 7, 1975, so the clause is spent: the effective-date statement has run and the revocation was carried out on issuance. The order was signed October 7, 1975 and printed at 40 FR 47469 on October 9, 1975; the signing date is used because the order says it is effective immediately. No later event is needed for this end.

research_rationale:
basis_pattern: original_plus_bounded_search. EO 11884 (signed 1975-10-07; 40 FR 47469; official Federal Register text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_11884.txt, read in full) prescribes the official Coat of Arms, Seal and Color and Flag of the Vice President of the United States and revokes Executive Order No. 10016. Identity: the heading of Executive Order 11884 of October 7, 1975, prescribing the official coat of arms, seal and flag of the Vice President at 40 FR 47469, the title and the date agree with the register row. The dossier inventory has one clause for the whole operative text, so I replaced it with five clauses (inventory override): sections 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5; section 5 is the effective-date and revocation section. Own terms: sections 1 to 4 have no end date or ending condition; section 5 is a self-executing effective-date and revocation provision performed on issuance, recorded as terminated on 1975-10-07. Later instruments: a search of every held order text for the number 11884 finds only the 1989 codification snapshot (and the order's own Federal Register copy); the dossier chain has no event and lists no actor. No held text revokes, supersedes or amends the order. The three selected machine searches (current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr, later-events:ofr_catalog) were read with their coverage notes, carry no coverage warning, and record 0, 0 and 0 hits for the order number respectively. Limit stated plainly: the continuing predicate for sections 1 to 4 rests on the held original text and the bounded searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09); the attached illustrations and specifications at 40 FR 47470 are image pages whose graphic content is not read here.
